status: Concept direction selected by Jordan; generated size study is not a production sprite atlas.
selected_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW comparative art-direction study derived from the supplied original Stead creature concept sheet. The reference is the approved character/material baseline, not a layout to replicate mechanically. These are original fantastical desktop companions, not conventional animals wearing accessories. Create one polished landscape board, 3 columns by 2 rows, with SIX fully visible creatures, generous breathing room, consistent apparent body scale, uncluttered warm ivory background. Small elegant labels only: the board title specified below and the six names. Each cell includes its main expressive three-quarter/full-body pose plus a small clearly related simplified silhouette thumbnail in a corner, to judge whether its identity survives reduction. Main figures still pixel-art with deliberately stepped contours, selective hand-placed pixel clusters, restrained coherent earthy palette, warm dark outlines; no photorealism, no vector/smooth gradients, no glossy 3D, no UI cards, no buildings or scenic backdrops, no random accessories.
The exact six identities and reading order:
Top left FOLIO: slim cream little dragon, big expressive moss-green leaf wings with warm vein lines and small torn/notched edges, longer elegant snout, springy tail, listening posture; preserve the leaflike specificity from original reference top-right, NOT a generic purple dragon.
Top middle TESSERA: squat six-legged ceramic beetle creature, three or more overlapping warm ivory porcelain shell plates, irregular deep teal botanical inlay/patterns, discreet hairline repairs, spindly articulate feet. Clear negative-space leg rhythm.
Top right CAIRN: three unequal floating sandstone stones, chipped warm facets, offset balance, tufts of moss, distinctive large irregular hole through middle stone. Actual sky/background through the hole, NOT three interchangeable blue blobs.
Bottom left PURL: small cuttlefish with teal mantle and ochre bands, large alert off-center eye, expressive fins and a few distinct curling arms, curious rather than menacing.
Bottom middle HUSH: imperfect weathered stone hoop with tufts of moss holding a contained plum-gray storm cloud, one quiet lightning zigzag, no generic face or legs. Open ring and cloud remain separately readable.
Bottom right KNOT: living ochre/russet woven ribbon with a clear large empty loop, two asymmetrical flowing ends forming stance, visible weave/pattern only in chosen areas, no eyes or added limbs.
Retain coherent stylistic family but independently authored silhouettes. Do not make every creature stand upright, give everything a face, or round them into plush mascots. No invented names, no watermark.
Board title (exact): "B · Bold little legends". Art direction: intentionally bolder compact authored pixel shapes, strong graphic negative space and surprising proportions. Fewer larger decisive material color clusters than A, roughly 80-100 pixel character height visually before clean enlargement, crisp stepped contours, richer local colors and confident contrasting planes. Preserve porcelain botany, hole in Cairn, leaf venation, woven loop, weather ring and cuttlefish bands as large legible distinguishing marks. Exaggerate each defining silhouette differently instead of using a universal cute face/body. Minimal selective dither; no smooth antialiasing. Feel like unforgettable peculiar creatures in a richly authored adventure game. Keep each small silhouette recognizably unusual.
size_study_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Edit/recompose the attached SELECTED art-direction board "B · Bold little legends" into a focused comparative small-size design study. The user chose this exact art style over softer, grainier or more acting-led alternatives. Preserve B's bold warm near-black contours, large confident pixel color clusters, cream/moss/teal/ochre material relationships, clear negative space and specific forms. Do not soften, make painterly, add generic purple, or revert to smooth geometric primitives.
New landscape sheet with THREE equal columns on the same warm ivory paper background. Title exactly "B · Courtyard-size study". Columns labeled FOLIO, TESSERA, CAIRN.
Each column shows ONE large main pose matching the selected reference and directly below it ONE genuinely small, separately simplified pixel redraw of that SAME pose. Large version ~350px tall; the small redraw ~90px tall within the final sheet and visibly a fraction of the main pose, lots of blank space around it. Beneath the large rows use small label "Material & silhouette"; beneath the small redraw row use "Small-size character". The little versions must visibly use fewer larger purposeful pixel clusters; not just a smooth downsample or an unfilled silhouette. They should preserve the visual idea with two or three bold material marks. All images fully in view.
FOLIO: poised cream dragon, long narrow snout and S-neck; paired large olive leaf wings with gold branching midribs and naturally notched edges, clear daylight gap between head and wings, teal mottling on flank, low curled tail. Main silhouette matching B, NOT earlier paper-wing purple sprite. Small redraw retains paired green leaf masses, a forked gold midrib per wing, cream face and throat, one teal flank mark, deliberate wing-to-neck gap.
TESSERA: one squat dome made from overlapping irregular warm ivory ceramic plates with bold blue-green botanical sprigs and a few repair seams. Six jointed legs emerge beneath overhanging scalloped plate rims. Small redraw retains ONE coherent overhanging shell, three broad ivory plates, two boldly readable teal sprigs, a few differently angled articulated feet and real gaps beneath shell; do not turn shell into disconnected blue discs.
CAIRN: 3 unequal floating sandstone stones in exact B mass order: broad tilted top slab, broad off-axis MIDDLE stone with a conspicuous actual transparent-through hole showing the page, small inverted pointed shard underneath. Moss grows on selected upper edges. Small redraw retains the irregular hole, canted top, tiny lower point and two moss patches; do not replace with stacked centered pebbles.
Keep the strong selected B style in both scales. No scenery, UI chrome, sprite-sheet grid, animation frames, technical claims, watermark, extra characters or silhouette inserts. This is an art proof, not a finished production sprite atlas.
